The main culprit was N+1 queries against PostgreSQL. The rate-quote path was firing a separate query per lane, so the work scaled with the number of lanes in a request instead of staying flat. I replaced that with a batched loader that pulls all the lanes in one round trip, and put a 90-second Redis cache in front of it keyed by lane ID. Together that took p95 from 820 ms down to 190 ms.

The outbox is what makes that safe. The status update and the outbox row go into the same PostgreSQL transaction, so either both commit or neither does. If the service dies halfway, the row is still unpublished, and the relay picks it up on the next poll and publishes it. The relay is at-least-once, so consumers dedupe on event_id in a processed_events table inside their own transaction.

Dockhand is the Kafka pipeline I built at Larkspur Freight to carry shipment status events, about 2.3 million a day. The core problem was dual writes: a carrier service would commit to Postgres and then call downstream over HTTP, so a crash in between lost the update and a retry duplicated it. We fixed it with a transactional outbox, a Go relay publishing to Kafka, and consumer-side dedupe on event_id. Duplicate delivered events hitting billing went to zero.
